question: Which of the following organisations, founded in 1875, opposes idol worship and supports the infallibility of the Vedas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Arya Samaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Arya Samaj**
 
• Arya Samaj is a Hindu reform movement founded by 'Swami Dayanand Saraswati'.
 
 
• Dayanand Saraswati had inspired the Arya Samaj from Swami Virjanand of Mathura in Bombay in 1875.
 
• Arya Samaji believed in pure Vedic tradition and rejected idol worship, avatars, sacrifice, false rituals, and superstitions.
 
• In this, untouchability and caste discrimination were opposed and women and Shudras were also given the right to wear Yagyopaveet and read the Vedas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Paramhansa Mandali​**

 
 
• In 1849, a covert socio-religious organization called the Paramhansa Mandali was founded in Bombay.
 
• It shares a tight relationship with Manav Dharma Sabha, which was established in Surat in 1844.
 
• Dadoba Pandurang, Durgaram Mehtaji, and several of his friends founded it.
 
• After leaving Manav Dharma Sabha, Dadoba Pandurang became the organization's leader.
 
• In 1848, he provided a summary of his beliefs in "Paramhansik Bramhyadharma" for Paramahansa Mandali and "Dharma Vivechan" for Manav Dharma Sabha.
 
• It functioned as a covert organization, and it's thought that when its existence was made public in 1860, it hastened its downfall.
 
• It was Maharashtra's first socioreligious institution.
 
• These Mandli's founders held a monotheistic belief.
 
• They were mostly concerned with disobeying caste laws.
 
• The members consumed food prepared by members of lower castes during their sessions.
 
• The mandali supported widow remarriage and women's education.
 
 
 
• **​Prayer Society**
 
 
• Prarthana Samaj was founded by Atmaram Pandurang on 31 March 1867 when Keshub Chandra Sen visited Maharashtra, intending to make people believe in one God and worship only one God. It became popular after Mahadev Govind Ranade joined.
 
• The Samaj was different from the Brahmo Samaj of Bengal in that it was not as radical and took a cautious approach to the reformist programmes. For this reason, it was better received by the public as well. The members were all Hindus and remained so throughout. They wanted to reform the religion from within.
 
• Prarthana Samaj, or "Prayer Society" in Sanskrit, was a movement for religious and social reform in Bombay based on earlier reform movements. Prarthana Samaj was founded by Atmaram Pandurang with the help of Keshav Chandra Sen in 1867, to make people believe in one God and worship only one God.
 
 
 
• **Ramakrishna Mission**
 
 
• Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897.
 
• The mission is named after his guru, Swami Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.
 
• The mission's main aim is to promote the teachings of Vedanta and work towards social welfare.
 
• It has played a significant role in the spiritual and cultural revival of India.
